first_impression.reaction: Googled 'name change after marriage' because my partner is weighing up taking my surname and wants to know what it actually involves. The first paragraph gives me a date stamp and the rule: married in Australia, the official certificate does it, no formal change of name. That's the answer. Then there's a Concierge link in paragraph two before the page has proved anything, so my guard went up. I went straight to the FAQ, then the step-by-step, the passport section and the overseas bit. Nearly every claim is pinned to a named agency with a link I can check, and it flags the catches (ceremonial certificate not accepted, foreign certificate may not prove a name change). The one gap for me is that the licence step is NSW only, and we're in Brisbane.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, if you married in Australia, NSW, Victoria and Queensland all let you do that with your official marriage certificate, without a formal change of name.
journey.reaction: Dated, specific, names the states. Queensland's in there, which is the one I care about. Good start.

journey.quote: When the paperwork has a plan, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=name-change-after-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration itself.
journey.reaction: Sales link in the second paragraph, before any evidence. It's conditional and polite, but I'm here for a government process, not a planner. Facts first, then ask.

journey.quote: It depends on your certificate and how many organisations you tell, so ask the registry for current timing when you order.
journey.reaction: Not a number, but at least it doesn't make one up. Honest beats a guessed timeframe.

journey.quote: If you married in Australia, NSW says you don't need to pay the fee for an official change of name.
journey.reaction: The useful bit is that you can skip the fee entirely if you married here. I'll check the registry for the actual amounts myself; I'd rather that than a figure that goes stale.

journey.section: How to change your name after marriage, step by step
journey.quote: Each new card becomes proof for the next organisation.
journey.reaction: That's the logic of the order explained, not just asserted. Makes sense.

journey.section: Step 1: Get the official registry marriage certificate (not the ceremonial one)
journey.quote: Centrelink does not accept them as a supporting document for a legal name change either.
journey.reaction: This is the catch nobody tells you. Three agencies saying the same thing. I'd have walked into a service centre with the pretty one.

journey.section: Step 1: Get the official registry marriage certificate (not the ceremonial one)
journey.quote: The Attorney-General's Department says your celebrant can apply for it on your behalf, generally at a cost, and that you will need it to change your name or prove you are married.
journey.reaction: Flags that there's a cost rather than pretending it's free. Fine.

journey.section: Step 2: Update your photo ID first (driver licence)
journey.quote: In other states, check with your state's transport agency for its process and documents.
journey.reaction: We're in Queensland. The page told me Queensland lets you use the certificate, then the actual licence step only covers Service NSW. Honest about the limit, but it leaves me to go and find the Queensland process myself.

journey.quote: By this point you hold what you need: NSW says your marriage certificate, new driver licence and new Medicare card will provide the proof in most cases.
journey.reaction: Sourced, and 'in most cases' is the honest qualifier. But again it's NSW's word. Does that hold in Queensland? Probably, but the page doesn't say.

journey.section: Step 6: Work, professional registrations and everything else
journey.quote: The tail of the list is long but quick.
journey.reaction: 'Quick' according to whom? Anyone who's tried to change details with a bank or a super fund knows it isn't always. Unsourced reassurance.

journey.section: Changing your name on your passport after marriage
journey.quote: It recommends booking travel in the name that's in your passport.
journey.reaction: Straight from the Passport Office and directly useful. That's the rule I'd have got wrong.

journey.section: Changing a first or middle name
journey.quote: NSW lists three surname options that work with a marriage certificate; every other change, including moving your surname into your middle names, goes through a formal application.
journey.reaction: The heading says first or middle name, but the text only really covers middle names. I worked out 'every other change' includes first names, but it took a second read.

journey.quote: In Tasmania and the Northern Territory, check with the registry before you start.
journey.reaction: Admits it doesn't cover those. I respect that more than a made-up summary.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: Smartraveller says a foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage, but you may be unable to use it as proof of a name change.
journey.reaction: That's the real catch with a wedding abroad, and it's sourced. If we went overseas, this is the thing that would bite.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact; the name change and every certificate stay with you and the official agencies.
journey.reaction: Good that they say what they don't do. But 'payments' again, with nothing about whether they take a cut from the vendors those payments go to.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the only line on the page that speaks to my actual worry about planners. That goes in the spreadsheet.

journey.quote: Once you know which certificate you will come home with, the rest is the part your guests remember.
journey.reaction: Brochure voice. Harmless. I skip it.

unanswered_questions: What's the Queensland process for updating a driver licence after marriage: where do you go and what do you bring? The page only covers Service NSW.
Does the NSW line about the certificate, new licence and new Medicare card being enough proof for banks and super hold in Queensland too?
Can you change a first name using the marriage certificate, or is that always a formal application? The heading promises it but the text only spells out middle names.
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or vendors whose payments it handles? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real destination wedding you've planned, with the actual budget, where the couple sorted the name change afterwards?

turn_offs_found.quote: When the paperwork has a plan, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=name-change-after-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration itself.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA in the second paragraph, before any evidence. I came for a government process, and getting a sales link before the sources makes me wonder what the page is really for.

turn_offs_found.quote: The tail of the list is long but quick.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsourced reassurance on a page that otherwise cites everything. 'Quick' is a promise nobody can back up for banks and super funds, and one padded line makes me check the rest harder.

turn_offs_found.quote: Once you know which certificate you will come home with, the rest is the part your guests remember.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sales copy instead of facts. It's the bit I scroll past to find the actual terms.

would_share_with: My partner, the step-by-step order and the ceremonial certificate warning, before she books anything at a service centre
My partner, the passport section, because the honeymoon is booked and the tickets need to match the passport she travels on

cta_reaction.why: The page earned some credit: dated, sourced, points me to the agencies instead of asking me to trust them, and says plainly that the name change isn't theirs. 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right line. But I came for a paperwork answer, not a planner, and my main question, whether they take a cut from the vendors whose payments they handle, isn't answered. They go in the comparison spreadsheet. I wouldn't enquire off this page alone.

top_3_changes: Cover Queensland (and ideally Victoria) in the driver licence step, or link to each state transport agency, instead of only 'In other states, check with your state's transport agency for its process and documents.'

Move the intro Concierge link below the key takeaways or into the overseas section, so the facts come before the ask: 'When the paperwork has a plan, Wedded Concierge can take on the celebration itself.'
Cut or source 'The tail of the list is long but quick.', and make the 'Changing a first or middle name' section say directly whether a first name change needs a formal application.

No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold the Queensland (TMR) licence update process or a Queensland equivalent of the NSW 'certificate, licence and Medicare card are proof in most cases' line? Either would close the main gap for a Brisbane reader.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'name change after marriage' while comparing three planners, checking the process for his partner, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood is 2.
Missing fee amounts are deliberate and not penalised; the registry fee mention without a figure is accepted.
The 5-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, step-by-step, passport and overseas sections in full and a skim of the state-by-state and reverting sections.
